extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions constructed using a novel crowdsourcing method that leverages domain-specific text and model suggestions for document selection and answer distractor choice.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected using a two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. First, workers selected from candidate textbook passages and formulated questions. Second, workers selected or generated answer distractors, aided by a random forest model trained to predict plausible distractors. The process involved 175 workers with Master's status.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to the base corpus to select relevant paragraphs. A random forest classifier was used to rank and suggest answer distractors. The dataset was split into training, validation, and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text was filtered using lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity-based rules to identify simple declarative statements. Questions were filtered for length (6-30 words), answer length (up to 3 words), and ambiguity. Distractors were validated for grammatical consistency and semantic relevance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk generated questions from provided passages and selected or wrote answer distractors. Workers were required to have Master's status. They were provided with model-generated distractor suggestions to aid in selection or generation. Quality control involved filtering out ungrammatical, false, or irrelevant questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Workers identified the crowdsourced questions as indistinguishable from original exam questions in a blind test (55% identification rate, not statistically significant). The distractor model achieved 94.2% validation accuracy, but human validation was still required to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 crowd workers with Amazon Mechanical Turk Master's status.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Random forest classifier (scikit-learn) for distractor ranking; GloVe embeddings; WordNet; OpenIE triples.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve science exam QA systems, which require mastery of information extraction, reading comprehension, and common sense reasoning. It addresses the bottleneck of lacking large in-domain training sets for science QA.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from science study textbooks, which may reflect the biases present in those educational materials. The questions are targeted at elementary to college introductory level science.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of multiple choice questions which may be trivial to answer if the supporting passage is provided (though the multiple choice version does not include the passage). Neural models did not outperform simple information retrieval baselines on the multiple choice version. Some passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, limiting the direct answer version.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for science exam question answering, reading comprehension, and natural language inference tasks.
